title: Attention-based neural machine translation
text: We propose an encoder-decoder model with attention for translating sentences between languages. The model improves BLEU scores on English to German translation compared with phrase-based systems.

title: Transformer models for sequence transduction
text: A transformer architecture based solely on self-attention is applied to machine translation. Training is faster than recurrent networks and translation quality improves on standard benchmarks.

title: Low-resource neural translation with back-translation
text: Back-translation augments scarce parallel data with synthetic sentences generated by a reverse translation model. We show gains for translating into morphologically rich languages.

title: Evaluating machine translation quality
text: We study automatic metrics such as BLEU and correlate them with human judgments of translation adequacy and fluency across several language pairs.

title: Semi-supervised node classification with graph convolutional networks
text: We introduce a graph convolutional network that propagates features along edges to classify nodes in citation graphs with few labeled examples.

title: Inductive representation learning on large graphs
text: We present a method that samples and aggregates neighborhood features to generate node embeddings for unseen nodes in large evolving graphs.

title: Graph attention networks
text: Attention coefficients over neighboring nodes let graph neural networks assign different importance to neighbors without costly matrix operations.

title: Link prediction in social networks
text: We compare heuristics and learned embeddings for predicting missing links between users in social graphs using network structure.

title: Dense passage retrieval for open-domain question answering
text: A dual encoder maps questions and passages into a shared vector space so that relevant passages can be found with nearest neighbor search, outperforming BM25.

title: Neural ranking models for document search
text: We survey neural ranking architectures that learn relevance between queries and documents, including interaction based and representation based models.

title: Query expansion with pseudo relevance feedback
text: Terms from top ranked documents are added to the original query to reduce vocabulary mismatch and improve recall in ad hoc retrieval.

title: Efficient indexing for approximate nearest neighbor search
text: We design an index that supports fast similarity search over millions of embedding vectors with small memory footprint.

title: Unsupervised keyphrase extraction with graph ranking
text: A graph of candidate phrases is ranked with a random walk to select the most important keyphrases from scientific documents.

title: Keyphrase generation with sequence to sequence models
text: An encoder-decoder model generates keyphrases that appear in the text as well as absent keyphrases that do not occur in the source document.

title: Statistical keyword extraction from single documents
text: We extract keywords using local statistical features such as casing, position and word frequency, without training data or dictionaries.

title: Keyphrases improve document indexing for search
text: Automatically extracted keyphrases are added to the index of scientific articles and improve retrieval effectiveness compared with full text only.

title: Communication-efficient federated learning of deep networks
text: Clients train models locally on private data and a server averages the updates, reducing communication while keeping raw data on devices.

title: Differential privacy in distributed model training
text: We add calibrated noise to gradients so that trained models provide formal privacy guarantees for individual training examples.

title: Attacks on federated learning systems
text: Malicious participants can poison model updates or infer private information from shared gradients in collaborative training.

title: Secure aggregation for privacy preserving learning
text: Cryptographic protocols let a server compute the sum of client updates without seeing any individual update.

title: U-Net for biomedical image segmentation
text: A convolutional network with skip connections segments cells and organs in microscopy and medical scans using few annotated images.

title: Deep learning for tumor segmentation in MRI
text: We train three dimensional networks to delineate brain tumors in magnetic resonance images and evaluate overlap with expert annotations.

title: Data augmentation for small medical datasets
text: Elastic deformations and intensity transformations enlarge small annotated datasets and improve generalization of segmentation models.

title: Evaluating segmentation overlap metrics
text: The Dice coefficient and Hausdorff distance are compared as measures of agreement between automatic and manual segmentations.
